headline: The bridge relay is RUNNING and healthy; the failure is NOT transport. /health answers 200 on two ports with edaConnected:false and /eda-windows returns an empty list. t53's 'BRIDGE_UNREACHABLE' is a mislabel: its discover() catch-all maps SCHEMATIC_BRIDGE_NO_EDA (relay up, no editor registered) onto that same string. Root cause is branch (b): the relay is up but no editor window is registered, so the registration step in the editor's own browser has not happened.

verbatim: bridge.ts L21-22: `/** First port the run-api-gateway bridge listens on (protocol constant). */` / `export const EASYEDA_BRIDGE_PORT_MIN = 49620`
bridge.ts L25-28: `Last port scanned for a run-api-gateway bridge.` / `export const EASYEDA_BRIDGE_PORT_MAX = 49630`
bin L69-72: `// The editor's built-in run-api-gateway hard-codes ws://127.0.0.1:49630 and` ... `const BUILTIN_GATEWAY_PORT = 49630`
portRange.whyTwoListeners: bin L18-22: `Port range 49620-49629; the first free port is picked at startup. A second listener binds 49630, the fixed endpoint the editor's built-in run-api-gateway dials after an api/landing?port= BroadcastChannel trigger (the port param is metadata only — the gateway always uses 49630)`. So 49620 + 49630 listening is ONE instance, not two daemons. I initially suspected two daemons; bin L18-22 corrects that.

layers.verdict: DISCREPANCY WITH THE TASK'S PREMISE, stated plainly: the response is 503, not 500, and the body is NOT the EASYEDA_BRIDGE_REGISTER_HINT text. The hint string lives in bridge.ts and is composed client-side into SchematicError messages; the relay itself returns this short JSON error. So the task's sub-step (c) 'confirm the body is the REGISTER_HINT sentence' cannot be confirmed - it is not that sentence. The 503 does independently prove the relay has no editor window.
layers.hintTextQuotedVerbatimForComparison: bridge.ts L47: `open https://pro.lceda.cn/api/landing?port=49620 as a NEW TAB IN THE SAME BROWSER that holds the web editor tab, after that editor tab has finished loading — a different browser, or opening it before the editor, leaves the relay with no window; opening a document only works once the relay is attached to the window that has the project loaded (its schematic page list is non-empty, and a landing-only window answers HTTP 500 to every call), and to bring an already-open schematic to the front double-click its document node in the project tree, because activateDocument does not change the visible tab`
layers.note: the hint text itself mentions 'a landing-only window answers HTTP 500 to every call' - that is a different condition (a window that registered but has no project loaded) and is not what we observe (zero windows at all, 503)

layers.verdict: BOUNDARY, reported honestly: I could NOT read the owning PID. The workspace sandbox denied Get-NetTCPConnection, Get-CimInstance and netstat. What is still proven without them: a listener exists on 49620 and 49630 (layer a: TCP connect succeeds) and it is this implementation (layer b: /health returns service=easyeda-bridge, bridge=dsh-eda-bridge). Only the PID is unknown.
layers.doNotConclude: do not read this as 'no listener'. An earlier attempt printed nothing for Get-NetTCPConnection because it raised and the error was suppressed; the TCP probe is the reliable evidence.

rootCause.statement: The relay process is up and healthy, but zero editor windows are registered with it (edaConnected:false, edaWindowCount:0, /eda-windows returns {"windows":[],"activeWindowId":null,"count":0}). Registration happens when the EasyEDA editor page, loaded in a browser that can reach the relay's BroadcastChannel, posts its registration; that has not happened for this relay instance.
rootCause.whyNotA: branch (a) requires no listener; TCP connect to 49620 and 49630 succeeds and /health answers 200.
rootCause.whyNotC: branch (c) requires a timeout or protocol mismatch; every request returned immediately (200/503/404), the service id and implementation id match bridge.ts exactly, and there is no SCHEMATIC_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT.
falsifiablePredictions: If an editor window registers, GET /health must flip to edaConnected:true and edaWindowCount>=1 within one heartbeat, and GET /eda-windows must list it. (Test: poll /health while the editor registers.)

If the relay is restarted and the editor page is not reloaded, edaWindowCount must stay 0 - because the page's gateway socket died with the old relay. (Test: restart the bin, observe count stays 0 until the page re-registers.)

If a browser other than the one holding the editor tab opens the landing URL, edaWindowCount must stay 0 - bridge.ts L47 says a different browser leaves the relay with no window. (Test: open the landing URL in a second browser profile and observe no registration.)

secondaryFinding.what: t53 reports this condition as BRIDGE_UNREACHABLE, which reads as 'the bridge is dead/transport unreachable'. It is not.
verbatim: t53-verify-main.mjs L106-108: `bridge = await HttpEasyEdaBridge.discover({ timeoutMs: 15_000 })` then `} catch (e) { fail('BRIDGE_UNREACHABLE', String((e && e.message) || e).slice(0, 200)) }`

t53-verify-main.mjs L129: `if (/NO_EDA|not connected|edaConnected/i.test(msg)) fail('EDA_NOT_CONNECTED', msg)` - this distinct label is unreachable for the NO_EDA case, because discover() throws before execute() runs
secondaryFinding.effect: the discover() catch-all collapses SCHEMATIC_BRIDGE_NO_EDA into BRIDGE_UNREACHABLE, so the session has been treating a registration problem as a dead transport for many rounds
secondaryFinding.fixSuggestion: classify the discover() error by its .code (SCHEMATIC_BRIDGE_NO_EDA -> EDA_NOT_CONNECTED, SCHEMATIC_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE -> BRIDGE_UNREACHABLE) instead of one catch-all string
